newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo! extends alliance with Visa, splits stock.
newsitem.headline: Yahoo! extends alliance with Visa, splits stock.

text.p: Yahoo! Inc said Tuesday it has formed a global electronic commerce alliance with Visa International and restated its second quarter results to reflect a $21,245,000 one-time charge.

The Internet search and navigation company said it had issued 466,321 shares of Yahoo! common stock to the Visa Group and has recorded the related one-time, non-cash pre-tax charge in its second quarter to June 30.

In exchange for the stake in Yahoo!, the Visa Group has agreed to release claims to its 45 percent ownership of a limited liability company, Yahoo! Marketplace LLC, which the two had set up as a joint venture.

"There is an emerging opportunity for commerce on the web and this agreement allows Yahoo! flexibility in aggressively pursuing this opportunity, while retaining 100 percent of the financial benefit for Yahoo! shareholders," Yahoo! Chief Financial Officer Tim Koogle said in a statement.

Yahoo!, based in Santa Clara, also said it was restating its second quarter results to show a net loss of $20.5 million, or $0.74 a share, compared to a net loss of $1.3 million, or $0.05 a share in second quarter 1996.
Excluding the one-time, non-cash charge, net income for the second quarter to June 30 was $610,000, or $0.02 a share, as previously reported on July 9.
Revenue totalled $13.5 million, up from $3.2 million a year earler, as previously reported.
Yahoo! also said its board approved a three-for-two stock split. Shareholders of record on August 11 will be entitled tor one additional share for every two shares held on that date.
Visa International and Yahoo! said they have formed a new strategic alliance to "aggressively extend their commerce- related activities on the Internet."

Yahoo! Senior Vice President Jeff Mallett said the agreement will enable Yahoo! and Visa to create co-branded shopping guides, a co-branded Yahoo! Visa card and joint promotions of the two brands through online and offline media.
Visa, which is comprised of 21,000 member financial institutions, has nearly 600 million cards, accepted at more than 14 million worldwide locations.

"We will be threading shopping and commerce related services throughout the Yahoo! network," Mallett told Reuters. The company already has partnerships with a small group of merchants, including ETrade Group and Amazon.com and Mallett said it plans to roll out as many as a couple of dozen such merchant deals beginning this fall.
"Yahoo!'s job is to send informed, educated consumers to the front door of our merchant partners," he said.

Yahoo! will produce and develop the Visa Shopping Guide by Yahoo!," and align with an unnamed financial institution to launch a co-branded Visa card designed specifically for Internet users, the company said.
Visa will feature personal finance planning guides and purchase assistance tools on a Visa Shopping Guide by Yahoo!
Finally, Yahoo! will designate Visa as its "preferred card" and promote Visa throughout its Web sites and to on-line merchants worldwide.

Todd Chaffee, senior vice president of Visa International, said the credit card group has agreed to keep a portion of its stake in Yahoo! for a minimum of two years as a strategic investment, but he declined to elaborate on details.
"We think the co-branded card will be one of the biggest co-branded cards" that Visa offers, he said.
